claims.text: Ceramic or metallic powder compacts conventionally require high sintering temperatures for full densification.
Machine-learning optimization of sintering pressure, heating rate, and dwell time can reduce the temperature required for full densification.
Machine-learning-optimized sintering can preserve the final microstructure and material properties while lowering sintering temperature.
Pressure, heating rate, and dwell time are controllable SPS processing parameters.
Spark plasma sintering can be used to consolidate mechanically alloyed metallic powders.
SPS consolidation can be performed in a vacuum environment.
Enhanced diffusion and optimized interparticle neck formation promote efficient mass transport at reduced sintering temperatures.
A machine-learning model can identify a processing-parameter combination that lowers the activation-energy barrier for particle bonding and diffusion.
The optimized processing regime accelerates interparticle-neck formation.
Accelerated neck formation leads to complete densification at lower temperatures.
The optimized regime suppresses excessive grain growth and unwanted phase transformations.
Machine-learning optimization will produce a measurable reduction in the sintering temperature required for full densification.
The lower-temperature process will produce equal or improved mechanical properties relative to conventional high-temperature sintering.
Conventional SPS may use fixed high-temperature, pressure, heating-rate, and dwell-time settings without adaptive optimization.
The success of machine-learning optimization may be limited by powder uniformity and reproducibility.
The optimization model may require recalibration for different material systems or sintering atmospheres.
The magnitude of the achievable temperature reduction depends on the material system and the quality and range of the model's training data.
